sections.h2: Where is the Swain County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
The office is in the Courthouse Building at 101 Mitchell Street in Bryson City, NC 28713. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1183, Bryson City, NC 28713, and the county lists (828) 488-9273, extension 2205.

Hours are 8:30 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday. Marriage licenses are issued from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, a window the county prints separately, so allow for a slightly earlier cutoff on any counter service. The office also publishes an email address, RegisterofDeeds@swaincountync.gov, for questions before you travel.

Swain County is a large, thinly settled county. Census QuickFacts shows 14,024 people on 527.73 square miles of land, about 26.8 people per square mile. Everyone with a deed to record, whether the parcel is in town or on a mountain road, uses this one counter.

sections.h2: What does the Swain County register actually record?
sections.html:
The office records real property documents and also keeps the county's vital records. The county page lists the following recordings, which covers nearly everything a seller will meet:

  • Deeds, contracts, leases, mortgages and deeds of trust.
  • Cancellations of deeds of trust, maps and plats, and powers of attorney.
  • Assumed names, UCC filings, articles of incorporation and corporate mergers.
  • Bankruptcy orders, judgments, marriage settlements and military discharges.

The same office collects the revenue stamps, meaning the excise tax, on deeds being recorded. It also issues certified copies of birth, death and marriage certificates. Certified vital record copies are $10.00 each and uncertified copies $1.00 each, according to the county page. Those fees apply to vital records, so they are separate from the schedule for recording a deed.

sections.h2: How much will it cost me to record a deed in Swain County?
sections.html:
The charge follows the uniform state schedule in G.S. 161-10, with $26.00 covering the first 15 pages of an ordinary instrument and $4.00 for each page beyond that. The county page links a recording fee schedule and a document standards sheet, and you should read both before submitting a paper deed.

The statute says its listed fees are complete and exclusive and are collected before an instrument is filed. A seller rarely pays this fee directly, since the buyer's closing costs normally absorb recording of the deed and the lender's security instrument. Ask your closer to confirm who is responsible under your contract.

Fee items to expect when documents are recorded in Swain County

sections.h2: Who pays the deed stamps in a Swain County sale?
sections.html:
The seller owes the excise tax. G.S. 105-228.30 requires the transferor to pay the register before recording, and the rate is one dollar for every $500 of the price or value conveyed, counting a partial $500 as a full one.

In practice the figure shows up on your settlement statement and the closer sends it to the Bryson City office with the deed. Because the tax follows the price, ask for the exact line amount rather than estimating. For a parcel lying in more than one county, the register in the county with the greater value collects the tax.

Half of the receipts go to the county general fund. The other half, less refunds and an allowance, is remitted monthly to the Department of Revenue, and the county may keep 2% of the State portion.

sections.h2: What is the land like, and how does that affect a sale?
sections.html:
Swain County has a median value for owner-occupied homes of $207,000 for 2020 to 2024, per Census QuickFacts. Owner-occupancy is 72.7%, and median gross rent is $742. The county counted 8,951 housing units in July 2025 and 94 building permits in 2025.

QuickFacts also reports that 30.6% of residents identify as American Indian and Alaska Native alone, the highest share among the four counties in the table the Census page compares. If a tract has an unusual ownership history, ask your title company early what it needs to see.

Median household income is $52,349 and 22.0% of residents are 65 or older. A clean chain of title at the register speeds up any closing.

sections.h2: Can I search Swain County land records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The county provides a remote access site for land records with two modes. The full system lets you search by grantor or grantee name, instrument number, or book and page. The imaging system only retrieves deed book images when you enter a book and page.

The county warns that online records are unofficial and that the official records are kept at the register's office. For a legal certified copy of a recorded document, you still go through the office.

  • Search by name when you do not know the book and page.
  • Use book and page for a direct image of a known deed.
  • Take any reference from the online index to the counter if you need an official copy.

sections.h2: How does the Swain County tax office tie in with a sale?
sections.html:
The tax office sits in the same Courthouse Building, with a separate mailing address of P.O. Box 2321. It splits into an assessor side, which handles values and reappraisal, and a collections side, which handles payment and enforcement. Phone numbers run through (828) 488-9273.

Per the county tax page, bills for real estate and personal property are mailed in July and are due September 1, with interest starting after January 5 of the next year. State law backs this up: taxes can be paid at face value before January 6, then 2% applies from January 6 to February 1 and three-fourths of 1% per month after that, under G.S. 105-360.

The page says Swain County's last reappraisal took effect January 1, 2021, and that North Carolina counties must reappraise at least every eight years. Ask the assessor's office for the current schedule and for your parcel's value history. The county also describes a disabled veteran exclusion form and a property tax relief application, and the state exclusion for veterans is $45,000 of appraised value under G.S. 105-277.1C.

sections.h2: What should I check before a Swain County closing?
sections.html:
Confirm three things with your closer: that the deed matches the legal description, that the excise tax amount is on the statement, and that outstanding property tax is settled. Unpaid property tax is a lien on the parcel under G.S. 105-355, attached as of the listing date, so a clean payoff matters to the buyer.

  • Ask whether the buyer's lender needs a payoff letter from a prior mortgage.
  • Ask who will carry the signed deed to the register and by what date.
  • Request the recording book and page once the deed is filed.

If the house came to you through an estate, the clerk of superior court in the county where the owner lived handles small estate affidavits, and the statute allows them after 30 days from the date of death for personal property up to $20,000. Real property matters belong with an attorney.

faqs.q: What are the office hours for the Swain County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The office is open 8:30 am to 5:00 pm Monday through Friday, and marriage licenses are issued from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. The address is 101 Mitchell Street, Bryson City.

faqs.q: How do I search Swain County deeds online?
faqs.a: Use the county's remote access site, which offers a full system search by name, instrument number or book and page, plus an imaging-only mode. Those results are unofficial, so use the office for certified copies.

faqs.q: Who pays the excise tax when a Swain County house sells?
faqs.a: The seller pays it, to the register of deeds, before the deed is recorded. The rate is $1.00 for each $500.00 or fractional part of the value, under G.S. 105-228.30.

faqs.q: What does a certified vital record copy cost in Swain County?
faqs.a: Certified copies are $10.00 each and uncertified copies $1.00 each, according to the county page. These fees are for birth, death and marriage records, not deed recordings.

faqs.q: When are Swain County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due September 1, and the county says interest begins after January 5. Ask the tax office in the Courthouse Building for your exact bill.
